subject: physics_2
question_text: Distinguish between zener breakdown and Avalanche breakdown.

verification.note: The 2+2 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Paper-II bank the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers, so neither check was run. The five printed contrasts (doping, reverse voltage, depletion thickness, which diodes, mechanism) are all kept. One phrase is written more precisely than the book: the book's fifth avalanche point reads 'Due to sufficient electric field, disturbing of covalent bonds takes place', which does not say what makes avalanche different. The mechanism is collision — the field accelerates minority carriers until they knock electrons out of covalent bonds and the freed carriers repeat it — and that is what is written here. The depletion thickness figures follow the book: less than about one micron for zener breakdown, of the order of one micron for avalanche.

recall_prompt: Compare the two breakdowns point by point — doping, reverse voltage, depletion thickness, which diodes, and the mechanism.

steps.label: Zener breakdown
lines: 1) It occurs in heavily doped diodes.
2) It occurs at low reverse voltages.
3) The depletion layer is thin, less than
5) The strong electric field across the

lines.text: thin layer breaks the covalent bonds

steps.margin_note: Two marks. Heavy doping, low voltage, thin layer, direct bond breaking — those four carry the marks.
steps.why: Heavy doping is the root cause of every other point. It makes the depletion layer very thin, so even a small reverse voltage produces a very strong field across it, and that field pulls electrons straight out of the covalent bonds without any collision.
common_mistakes: Saying zener breakdown happens at high reverse voltage. It happens at low reverse voltage, below about 6 V.
Saying the diode is destroyed. Zener breakdown is not damage — the diode recovers, provided the current is limited by a series resistor.
Describing collisions. Collision is the avalanche mechanism, not the zener one.

recall.must_convey: That zener breakdown occurs in heavily doped diodes at low reverse voltage, across a thin depletion layer, by the field breaking covalent bonds directly.
accept: heavily doped and low reverse voltage
thin depletion layer under one micron
reject: lightly doped diodes at high voltage

steps.memory_tip: Zener: heavy doping, thin layer, low voltage, field pulls bonds apart.

steps.label: Avalanche breakdown
lines: 1) It occurs in lightly doped diodes.
2) It occurs at high reverse voltages.
3) The depletion layer is thicker, of the
5) The field speeds up the minority

lines.text: carriers until they collide and break
collide again, so the current builds up.

steps.margin_note: Two marks. Light doping, high voltage, thicker layer, and collisions — the word collision is what separates this from zener breakdown.
steps.why: Light doping makes the depletion layer wide, so a carrier crossing it is accelerated over a long distance and arrives with enough energy to knock an electron out of a bond by collision. Each collision makes two carriers where there was one, and the repeating process is what the word avalanche describes.
common_mistakes: Leaving out the collisions. That word is the whole difference from zener breakdown.
Saying it occurs only in zener diodes. It occurs in ordinary diodes as well.
Saying the depletion layer is thinner than in zener breakdown. It is thicker.

recall.must_convey: That avalanche breakdown occurs in lightly doped diodes at high reverse voltage, across a thicker layer, by accelerated carriers breaking bonds through collisions.
accept: lightly doped and high reverse voltage
reject: heavily doped diodes at low voltage

steps.memory_tip: Avalanche: light doping, wide layer, high voltage, one collision starts many.

insider_note: The examiner is looking for one word in each column — direct field for zener, collisions for avalanche. Everything else follows from the doping level.
